history.summary: The Naulakha Mandir was built in 1940 with a donation of nine lakh rupees by Rani Charushila Devi of the Pathuria Ghat royal family, Kolkata, who had lost her husband Akshay Ghosh and son Jatindra Ghosh at an early age. On the advice of the saint Balananda Brahmachari, she built the Radha-Krishna temple in his memory; the idol of Balananda Brahmachari is also venerated inside. The 146-foot red-sandstone tower is modelled on the Ramakrishna Temple at Belur Math. It stands ~1.5-2 km from Baba Baidyanath Temple at Karnibag. One weak source (velpu.com) claims an 8th-century origin renovated in 1940 - UNVERIFIED, treated as unreliable.

town_description: Deoghar, the 'Abode of Gods', is the cultural capital of Jharkhand and headquarters of Deoghar district in the Santhal Parganas division. It is primarily known for the Baidyanath Jyotirlinga, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas of Shiva, which makes it one of eastern India's busiest pilgrimage centres, especially during the Shravan month Kanwar Yatra. The city became a municipality in 1869 and is surrounded by small hills including Nandan Pahar, Trikut Pahar and Tapovan Pahar, with the Ajay river flowing nearby.
